sample: The validation sample: loan histories the life generator writes for this check, from a seed kept out of every training run and reported score. The same tests apply to a subservicer's own sample once one is in hand under terms counsel approves (docs/subservicer-data.md, What this means for synthetic data). Each test names the calibration key it checks, how the target is read from that key, and the smallest sample it means anything on.

tests.measure: Share of installments arriving in each of payment.day_of_month's bins, over installments due on loans current at the due date.

tolerance.reason: At 50,000 installments a bin's sampling error is at most 0.0023, so 0.02 is wide of noise and narrow enough to catch a bin drawn from the wrong day range.

tests.measure: Share of installments, on loans current at the due date, received after the due day and by the last day of grace.

tolerance.reason: The same reasoning as payment-arrival-day; this is three of its bins summed.

tests.measure: Late charges assessed per loan-year, counting loan-months that start current and leaving out months in which no late charge is owed (forbearance, bankruptcy, an SCRA waiver).

tolerance.reason: One late charge per installment not received by the end of grace. 5,000 loan-years give about 2,500 charges, a sampling error near 2%; 15% leaves room for the months left out.

tests.measure: Share of receipts short of the installment due.

tolerance.reason: About 500 events at the floor, a sampling error near 4.5%. Wide because the rate is itself a design choice; the test catches a generator that ignores it, not a few tenths of a point.

tests.measure: Share of receipts reversed after posting (a returned bank debit or check).

tolerance.reason: About 300 events at the floor, a sampling error near 6%; wide for the reason given under partial-payments.

tests.measure: Share of loan-months, on loans current at the due date, with no installment received by month end.

tolerance.reason: About 600 events at the floor, a sampling error near 4%. The public bounds on this rate are tested through delinquency-stock and quarterly-transitions.

tests.measure: Share of all loans 30, 60 and 90 or more days delinquent and not in foreclosure, at each quarter end after the first year of history.

target.compare: each bucket, averaged over quarter ends

tolerance.unit: absolute, each bucket; 0.01 on the total
tolerance.reason: The public level the monthly design choices (missed months, cures, rolls) have to land on. Half a point is a tenth of the total: close enough to place a book among real ones, loose enough for a sample's mix of loan types.

tests.measure: Share of conventional loans one payment or more past due and not in foreclosure, at each quarter end after the first year of history.

tolerance.reason: As delinquency-stock. A book of only conventional loans should sit near 2.7%, not near the all-loans 4.4% that FHA lifts.

tests.measure: Share of loans current at one quarter end that are 30-60 days late at the next, and share of loans 30-60 days late that are current at the next.

tolerance.unit: relative on the roll from current; 0.08 absolute on the cure
tolerance.reason: The New York Fed counts credit-report accounts, home equity installment loans among them, so a servicer's book need not match it closely; the test catches a monthly model whose quarterly arithmetic is off by a multiple.

tests.measure: Inbound contacts per loan-year, over all loans and by the loan's delinquency status in the month of the contact.

target.by_status_reason: The CFPB gives no split by status. These rise with delinquency, as early-intervention calls and loss-mitigation follow-up would, and over a book at delinquency.all_loans_30plus_share_sa's buckets and foreclosure inventory they average 2.0 a loan-year, the public figure.

tolerance.unit: absolute per loan-year on all loans; 25% relative on each status; current below d30 below d60 at or below d90_plus
tolerance.reason: The public figure is a 2021 pooled average across sixteen servicers that counted inquiries differently (1.9 to 2.08 by month), so 0.3 holds that spread and a little more.

tests.measure: Share by reason of the inbound contacts the sample marks as complaints or notices of error, mapped onto the key's twelve reasons.

tolerance.unit: absolute, each reason; the three largest reasons in the same order
tolerance.reason: Complaints are compared with complaints: the database is a skewed proxy for all calls and is not a target for routine ones. 2,000 contacts give a sampling error of at most 0.011 on a share.

tests.measure: Handle time recorded on each call, averaged over each month's calls, and the length in characters of each call's note.

target.compare: each month's average handle time inside [min, max]
target.notes_reason: No public source gives the length of a servicer's call notes; only a subservicer's sample can (docs/subservicer-data.md, kind 3). The band is a few sentences to a short paragraph.

tolerance.unit: minutes a month's average may fall outside [min, max]
tolerance.reason: The public range is of servicers' and call centers' monthly averages, so it bounds a month's average and not a single call: a two-minute call and a forty-minute one are both ordinary. Half a minute holds the noise in a month of a small sample.

tests.measure: Ledger transactions per loan-year on loans current at every due date of the year: receipts, curtailments, short and returned receipts and their reversals, late charges, and escrow disbursements.

target.late_charges: A loan current at every due date misses no month, so its late charges are the installments received from day 17 to month end, not payment.late_after_grace_share, which counts the missed month too.
target.escrow_disbursements_reason: Two property tax installments and one insurance premium; jurisdictions bill taxes once, twice or four times a year.

tolerance.reason: The twelve installments are most of the count, so a tenth catches a missing kind of transaction without failing on tax billing schedules.

tests.measure: Planted defects per eligible unit, by defect ID, read from the generator's manifest; and the share of planted defects the manifest labels.

tolerance.unit: confidence of the two-sided binomial interval each observed count must fall in, given the sample's count of eligible units; every planted defect labeled, exactly
tolerance.reason: The rates are design choices, so the test asks only that the generator plant what it says, at the rate it says, and label each one: an unlabeled defect cannot be graded.

tests.measure: Share of loans by note rate bucket at the sample's as-of date.

tolerance.reason: At 5,000 loans a bucket's sampling error is at most 0.007; 0.02 is three of those.

tests.measure: Share of loans by mark-to-market LTV bucket at the sample's as-of date.

tolerance.reason: As note-rate-distribution.

tests.measure: Share of loans by years since origination at the sample's as-of date.

tolerance.reason: As note-rate-distribution.

tests.measure: Share of loans that are adjustable-rate at the sample's as-of date.

tolerance.reason: At 4.3% and 5,000 loans the sampling error is 0.003; a point is three of those.

tests.measure: Share of loans with an escrow account for taxes at the sample's as-of date.

tolerance.reason: The target is itself a design choice until the ACS microdata share is computed; three points holds the generator to it without pretending to more.

tests.measure: Median yearly property tax and hazard insurance disbursed per escrowed loan, in the sample's newest full year.

tolerance.reason: The ACS medians are over all mortgaged owners in 2024 and the sample's year may differ, so a tenth; the growth keys say how far a later year should move.
